facts.statement: The name Camptosaurus means 'flexible lizard', derived from Greek words for 'bent' and 'lizard'.
facts.quote: The name means 'flexible lizard' (Greek καμπτος () meaning 'bent' and σαυρος () meaning 'lizard').

facts.statement: Camptosaurus was a plant-eating, beaked ornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic in western North America and possibly Europe.
facts.quote: Camptosaurus ( ) is an extinct genus of plant-eating, beaked ornithischian dinosaurs of the Late Jurassic period of western North America and possibly also Europe.

facts.statement: Remains of a small euornithopod were found by William Harlow Reed in Albany County, Wyoming, on September 4, 1879.
facts.quote: On September 4, 1879 William Harlow Reed in Albany County, Wyoming found the remains of a small euornithopod.

facts.statement: Marsh renamed the genus Camptosaurus in 1885 because the original name Camptonotus was already used for a cricket.
facts.quote: The genus was renamed Camptosaurus by him in 1885 because the original name was already in use for a cricket.

facts.statement: Marsh named the type species C. dispar in 1879 based on fossils from Quarry 13 near Como Bluff, Wyoming, and named C. amplus based on a foot found by Arthur Lakes at Quarry 1A.
facts.quote: In 1879, Marsh named C. dispar (type species of the genus) for material he received from his collectors at Quarry 13 near Como Bluff, Wyoming in the Morrison Formation and C. amplus based on the holotype YPM 1879, a foot found by Arthur Lakes at Quarry 1A.

facts.statement: The foot originally used to describe C. amplus was later determined to belong to Allosaurus.
facts.quote: The foot was later shown to have belonged to Allosaurus.

facts.statement: C. depressus was recovered from the Lakota Formation near Hot Springs, South Dakota.
facts.quote: Camptosaurus depressus was recovered from the Lakota Formation near the town of Hot Springs, South Dakota.

facts.statement: In 1980, Galton and Powell suggested that C. nanus, C. medius, and C. browni were different growth stages or genders of C. dispar, leaving only C. dispar as a valid species.
facts.quote: In 1980, Peter Galton and H.P. Powell in their redescription of C. prestwichi (see following), considered C. nanus, C. medius and C. browni to be different growth stages or different gender of the larger C. dispar, and therefore only C. dispar was a valid species.

facts.statement: In 2007, researchers placed a skull previously referred to C. amplus into its own genus and species, Theiophytalia kerri.
facts.quote: In 2007, they put it into its own genus and species, Theiophytalia kerri.

facts.statement: In 2022, Sánchez-Fenollosa et al. described the first confirmed European remains tentatively belonging to Camptosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2022, the first confirmed European remains belonging to aff. Camptosaurus .sp were described by Sánchez-Fenollosa et al..

facts.statement: Camptosaurus was a heavily built dinosaur with robust hindlimbs, broad four-toed feet.
facts.quote: Camptosaurus is a relatively heavily built form, with robust hindlimbs and broad feet, still having four toes.

facts.statement: The largest known fragments indicate that adult Camptosaurus could reach around 6.79 meters in length.
facts.quote: The largest fragments from later strata indicate adult individuals around 6.79 m long.

facts.statement: Camptosaurus typically reached 5 to 6 meters in length and weighed between 500 and 1000 kilograms.
facts.quote: It is estimated that Camptosaurus typically reached 5 - 6 m long and weighed 500 - 1000 kg.

facts.statement: Camptosaurus had teeth more tightly packed in its jaw compared to other euornithopods from the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: Its teeth were more tightly packed in the jaw compared to other Morrison euornithopods.

facts.statement: Extensive wear on Camptosaurus teeth indicates a diet of relatively tough vegetation.
facts.quote: Camptosaurus teeth frequently exhibit extensive wear, which indicates that individuals in the genus had a diet of relatively tough vegetation.

facts.statement: Marsh assigned Camptosaurus to its own family, Camptosauridae, in 1885.
facts.quote: Marsh in 1885 assigned Camptosaurus to a family of its own: the Camptosauridae.

facts.statement: Modern phylogenetics places Camptosaurus as a basal member of the clade Ankylopollexia.
facts.quote: Modern phylogenetics has made Camptosaurus by definition part of the clade Ankylopollexia, of which group it would then be a basal member.

facts.statement: Camptosaurus is closely related to the ancestors of later iguanodontids and hadrosaurids and is more derived than contemporaries like Dryosaurus and Nanosaurus.
facts.quote: This would mean that the genus is closely related to the ancestor of later iguanodontid and hadrosaurid dinosaurs and was more derived than contemporaries such as Dryosaurus and Nanosaurus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether C. prestwichii belongs in Camptosaurus; some researchers argue it should remain in the separate genus Cumnoria as it is more closely related to advanced iguanodonts.
facts.quote: However, Naish & Martill (2008), McDonald and colleagues (2010), and McDonald (2011) found that Seeley's original generic distinction was valid. Cumnoria has been recovered as a styracosternan, more closely related to advanced iguanodonts than to Camptosaurus dispar, similar to the case of Uteodon.

facts.statement: An analysis suggests C. aphanoecetes is more closely related to advanced iguanodonts, leading to its reclassification as Uteodon.
facts.quote: An analysis by Andrew McDonald and colleagues in 2010 suggested that like C. aphanoecetes is actually more closely related to more advanced iguanodonts (Styracosterna). It has been moved to the new genus Uteodon.

facts.statement: Specimens of C. dispar from Quarry 13 date to the Callovian-Oxfordian stages of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: The specimens with certainty belonging to Camptosaurus dispar, from Quarry 13, have been recovered from very deep layers, probably dating to the Callovian-Oxfordian.

facts.statement: Camptosaurus lived during the late Jurassic period, approximately between 160 and 145 million years ago, from the Oxfordian to the Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Jurásico, aproximadamente entre 160 millones de años a 145 millones de años, desde el Oxfordiense al Titoniense

facts.statement: Camptosaurus lived in what is now western North America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es el oeste de América del Norte

facts.statement: Camptosaurus was relatively stocky with robust hind limbs and large feet that possessed four toes.
facts.quote: Camptosaurus es relativamente corpulento, con extremidades posteriores robustas y grandes pies, que en estos poseía cuatro dedos

facts.statement: The largest fragments from later strata indicate that adult individuals averaged more than 7.9 meters in length and 2 meters in height.
facts.quote: Los fragmentos más grandes de los estratos posteriores indican que los individuos adultos median de más de 7,9 metros de largo y 2 metros de alto

facts.statement: Specimens from Quarry 13 were smaller, reaching lengths of 6 meters and weighing between 785 and 874 kilograms.
facts.quote: Pero los especímenes de la cantera 13 son más pequeños, llegando a medir 6 metros de longitud y pesando 785 a 874 kg de peso

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul provided a smaller estimate of a length of five meters and a weight of half a ton.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul dio una estimación aún menor, una longitud de cinco metros y un peso de media tonelada

facts.statement: The skull was actually triangular with a pointed snout equipped with a beak.
facts.quote: El cráneo era, de hecho, triangular con un hocico puntiagudo, equipado con un pico

facts.statement: Its teeth were packed more tightly in the jaw compared to other ornithopods from the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: Sus dientes estaban más apretujados en la mandíbula en comparación con otros ornitópodos de la formación Morrison

facts.statement: Camptosaurus possessed teeth that frequently exhibited significant wear, indicating that individuals in the genus had a diet of relatively tough vegetation.
facts.quote: Camptosaurus poseía dientes que con frecuencia exhiben un gran desgaste, lo que indica que los individuos en el género tenían una dieta de vegetación relativamente dura

facts.statement: On September 4, 1879, William Harlow Reed found the remains of a small ornithopod in Albany County, Wyoming.
facts.quote: El 4 de septiembre de 1879 William Harlow Reed encontró en el condado de Condado de Albany (Wyoming) los restos de un pequeño ornitópodo

facts.statement: That same year, Professor Othniel Charles Marsh described and named the find as Camptonotus, or "flexible spine".
facts.quote: Ese mismo año el profesor Othniel Charles Marsh describió y nombró el hallazgo como Camptonotus, o "espalda flexible"

facts.statement: The genus was renamed Camptosaurus, from Greek meaning "bent" and "lizard", "flexible lizard", by Marsh himself in 1885.
facts.quote: El género fue renombrado como Camptosaurus, del griego καμπτος/kamptos, 'doblado' y σαυρος/sauros , "lagarto", "lagarto flexible" por él mismo en 1885

facts.statement: In 1879, Marsh named C. dispar, the type species of the genus, for material received from collectors at Quarry 13 near Como Bluff, Wyoming, in the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: En 1879, Marsh nombró a C. dispar,la especie tipo del género, para el material que recibió de sus colectores en la Cantera 13, cerca de Como Bluff (Wyoming) en la formación Morrison

facts.statement: In 1980, Peter Galton and H.P. Powell considered that C. nanus, C. medius, and C. browni were different growth stages or sexes relative to the larger C. dispar.
facts.quote: En 1980, Peter Galton y H.P. Powell en su redescripción de C. prestwichi, consideraron que C. nanus, C. medius y C. browni eran de diferentes etapas de crecimiento o eran de diferente sexo con respecto al mayor C. dispar

facts.statement: In 2007, a skull previously referred to Camptosaurus was placed in its own genus and species, Theiophytalia kerri.
facts.quote: En 2007, fue situado en su propio género y especie, Theiophytalia kerri

facts.statement: Another species, Camptosaurus aphanoecetes, was named by Carpenter and Wilson in 2008 for specimens from Dinosaur National Monument.
facts.quote: Otra especie, Camptosaurus aphanoecetes, fue nombrada por Carpenter y Wilson en 2008 para los especímenes del Monumento nacional Dinosaurio

facts.statement: An analysis by Andrew McDonald and colleagues in 2010 suggested that C. aphanoecetes, as Cumnoria, is more closely related to advanced iguanodontians (Styracosterna).
facts.quote: Un análisis realizado por Andrew McDonald y colaboradores en 2010 sugirió que como Cumnoria, C. aphanoecetes está en realidad más estrechamente relacionado con los iguanodontes más avanzados (Styracosterna)

facts.statement: C. valdensis is a dubious driosaurid based on the holotype and only known specimen 'NHMUK R167', a poorly preserved left femur lacking the distal end.
facts.quote: C. valdensis es un dudoso driosáurido, basado en el holotipo y único espécimen conocido 'NHMUK R167', un fémur izquierdo mal conservado que carece del extremo distal

facts.statement: C. leedsi is probably a valid driosaurid that has been transferred to the new genus Callovosaurus.
facts.quote: C. leedsi es probablemente un driosáurido válido que ha sido trasladado al nuevo género Callovosaurus

facts.statement: C. hoggii was originally named Iguanodon hoggii by Richard Owen in 1874 and was transferred to Camptosaurus by Norman and Barrett in 2002.
facts.quote: C. hoggii fue originalmente llamado Iguanodon hoggii por Richard Owen en 1874 y fue trasladado a Camptosaurus por Norman y Barrett en 2002

facts.statement: Since then, C. hoggii has been transferred to the genus Owenodon.
facts.quote: Desde entonces ha sido transferido al género Owenodon

facts.statement: The remaining European species, Camptosaurus prestwichii, was recovered from brick quarries in Chawley, Cumnor Hurst, Oxfordshire, England.
facts.quote: La especie europea restante, Camptosaurus prestwichii fue recuperado de las canteras de ladrillo de Chawley, en Cumnor Hurst en Oxfordshire, Inglaterra

facts.statement: The fossil was found when a tram was pushed up the side of a hill.
facts.quote: El fósil fue encontrado cuando un tranvía fue impulsado en la ladera de una colina

facts.statement: It was described by Hulke in 1880 as Iguanodon prestwichii, and later placed in its own genus, Cumnoria, by Seeley in 1888.
facts.quote: Fue descrito por Hulke en 1880 como Iguanodon prestwichii, y luego se situó en su propio género, Cumnoria por Seeley en 1888

facts.statement: However, Naish and Martill (2008), McDonald and colleagues (2010), and McDonald (2011) found that the original generic distinction made by Seeley was valid.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Naish y Martill (2008), McDonald y colaboradores (2010) y McDonald (2011) encontraron que la distinción genérica original hecha por Seeley era válida

facts.statement: Alternatively, some authors considered it an early member of Iguanodontidae.
facts.quote: Alternativamente algunos autores lo consideraron un miembro temprano de Iguanodontidae

facts.statement: Modern phylogenetics has made Camptosaurus by definition part of the clade Ankylopollexia, where it would be a basal member.
facts.quote: La filogenética moderna ha hecho Camptosaurus por definición parte del clado Ankylopollexia, de cuyo grupo sería entonces un miembro basal

facts.statement: This would mean the genus is closely related to the ancestor of later iguanodontid and hadrosaurid dinosaurs and was more derived than contemporaries like Dryosaurus, Drinker, and Othnielosaurus.
facts.quote: Esto significaría que el género está estrechamente relacionado con el antepasado de los dinosaurios iguanodóntidos y hadrosáuridos posteriores y fue más derivado que contemporáneos como Dryosaurus, Drinker y Othnielosaurus

facts.statement: Some authors also consider it a member of the family Iguanodontidae, but this is a matter of debate.
facts.quote: También algunos autores consideran que es miembro de la familia Iguanodontidae pero esto es cuestión de debate

facts.statement: Museum curator John Foster described Camptosaurus with "medium to thick crests on its sides and lateral denticles along its edges," traits similar to but "more fully developed" than those of Dryosaurus.
facts.quote: El conservador del museo John Foster describe a Camptosaurus con "crestas medianas a gruesas en sus lados y dentículos laterales a lo largo de sus bordes," estos rasgos eran similares, pero "más plenamente desarrollados" que los de Dryosaurus

facts.statement: Specimens known with certainty to belong to Camptosaurus dispar from Quarry 13 have been recovered from deep layers that probably date from the Callovian to the Oxfordian.
facts.quote: Especímenes que se sabe con certeza que pertenecen a Camptosaurus dispar, de la cantera 13, se han recuperado de capas muy profundas, que probablemente datan del Calloviense al Oxfordiense

facts.statement: Due to the separate status of Uteodon, it has become problematic to determine which Morrison material belongs to Camptosaurus.
facts.quote: Debido al estado separado de Uteodon se ha convertido en problemático qué material de la Morrison pertenece a Camptosaurus

facts.statement: Scientists believe Camptosaurus could reach speeds of 25 km/h based on studies of other iguanodontians.
facts.quote: Con base en estudios de otros iguanodontes, los científicos creen que puede haber sido capaz de lograr velocidades de 25 km/h.

facts.statement: A fossilized embryo approximately 23 centimeters long attributed to Camptosaurus was recovered from the Morrison Formation at the Dinosaur National Monument in Utah.
facts.quote: Un pequeño embrión fosilizado de aproximadamente 23 centímetros, referido a Camptosaurus, fue recuperado de los estratos de la Formación Morrison en el Monumento nacional Dinosaurio en Utah.

facts.statement: Camptosaurus lived alongside theropods like Allosaurus and Ceratosaurus, sauropods like Apatosaurus and Diplodocus, and ornithischians like Dryosaurus and Stegosaurus in the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: Camptosaurus convivió con algunos dinosaurios terópodos como Allosaurus, Ceratosaurus, Ornitholestes y Torvosaurus, los saurópodos Apatosaurus, Brachiosaurus, Camarasaurus, y Diplodocus, y los ornitisquios Dryosaurus, y Stegosaurus los cuales han sido recolectados de la Formación Morrison.

facts.statement: Three species of Camptosaurus were found in the Morrison Formation across the US states of Colorado, Oklahoma, Utah, and Wyoming.
facts.quote: Tres especies son de América Norte de la Formación Morrison en los Estados Unidos, recolectados en los estados de Colorado, Oklahoma, Utah y Wyoming

facts.statement: The species C. pretswichii, found near Oxford and in Portugal, is considered the only certain evidence of the genus Camptosaurus outside North America.
facts.quote: la especie C. pretswichii, que se encontrado en lugares cerca de Oxford y en Portugal, es considerado como la única prueba indudable del género Camptosaurus fuera de América del Norte

facts.statement: The only theropod found in the deepest layers of the quarry was the relatively small Coelurus, which posed no threat to adult Camptosaurus.
facts.quote: El único terópodo de la cantera en la última capa del estrato es el relativamente pequeño Coelurus, que no constituía ninguna amenaza a un Camptosaurus adulto.
